headline: Youth Development exam questions sold for 10 lakh Taka; 7 arrested in paper leak scam
summary: A syndicate allegedly sold leaked exam questions for Tk 10 lakh, demanding original educational certificates or signed bank checks as collateral from job seekers. Seven individuals have been arrested in connection with the scam.
details: A syndicate involved in leaking questions for the Youth Development Directorate's Assistant Youth Development Officer recruitment exam allegedly demanded Tk 10 lakh for question papers and answers. They would take original educational certificates as collateral, which would only be returned upon full payment.

If job seekers couldn't pay upfront, the syndicate required signed blank bank checks, each valued at Tk 2-3 lakh. This method was revealed by investigating officers after interrogating arrested members of the ring.

The Special Response Battalion (SRB) arrested seven members of the syndicate in raids across Dhaka and its outskirts from Wednesday to Friday. Authorities seized 116 stamp papers, 10 educational certificates, 40 signed bank checks, and checkbooks from their possession.

The arrested individuals include Noor Mohammad (30), Jahangir (38), and S M Imdadul Islam (35) from the National Board of Revenue (NBR); Asadul Islam (33) from the Ministry of Defense; Md. Rubel Islam (33) from the Department of Environment; and two other syndicate members, Mofizul Islam (23) and Md. Hasinur Rahman alias Sujon. They have all been sent to jail.

Lieutenant Colonel Faizul Arefin, commander of SRB-3, stated that the syndicate made written agreements on stamp papers with job seekers. Original certificates were held until the full Tk 10 lakh was paid, or signed checks were taken for those unable to pay in advance.

Investigators are actively probing how the question papers reached the syndicate members and are working to identify and apprehend other individuals involved in the leak. The case has now been transferred to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).

According to investigation sources, NBR office assistant Noor Mohammad received a blurry image of the question paper at 4:43 AM on October 10. Later, NBR computer operator Jahangir received a clearer image around 6:15 AM, after which answers were prepared and distributed.
The Youth and Sports Ministry formed a five-member committee to investigate the leak, which has not yet submitted its report. Meanwhile, a new recruitment examination was conducted last Friday.

The original exam for 242 Assistant Youth Development Officer posts was scheduled for October 10, with 318,976 candidates eligible. The exam was suspended at 10:03 AM after news of the question paper leak spread, leading to a case filed by the Youth Development Directorate.

headline: Tk 4 crore Hilsa sold daily in Barisal despite ongoing ban
summary: Despite a 22-day ban to protect mother Hilsa, an estimated Tk 4 crore worth of Hilsa is illegally traded daily in Barisal's Meghna River. Organized groups are actively involved in fishing, buying, and selling.
details: An estimated Tk 3.5 to 4 crore worth of Hilsa is being bought and sold daily across eight ghats in Hizla, Barisal, despite a government ban to protect mother Hilsa. This illicit trade is occurring day and night in the remote char areas and estuaries of the Meghna River.

Local fishermen and traders indicate that a large syndicate is active in Hizla, orchestrating the illegal fishing, buying, selling, and smuggling of mother Hilsa during the ban. Numerous engine-powered trawlers and boats are used by fishermen to catch the fish.

Enforcement drives by the Coast Guard and fisheries officials have faced resistance, including two attacks since the ban began on October 8. In one incident, Coast Guard members fired 11 blank shots to control the situation after being attacked, while another team faced stone pelting, injuring a worker.

The areas of Janpur, Khalishpur, and Chorkilla in Meghna have become primary hubs for illegal Hilsa fishing and sales. Fishermen use 'fighter' trawlers equipped with multiple engines to evade authorities and are reportedly aggressive, attacking enforcement teams with bricks, stones, bamboo, sticks, and sharp weapons.

Fishermen claim that at least two thousand fishermen are operating large trawlers day and night, with each trawler carrying 20 to 30 individuals. Small boats can catch Tk 30,000-35,000 worth of Hilsa daily, while large trawlers net Tk 1.5-2 lakh.

Sources allege that several fishing ghats, crucial for this illegal trade, are controlled by politically influential individuals. These include leaders and members from both the Awami League and BNP, who reportedly take up to 20% commission on fish sales.

However, some accused individuals, including Altaf Hossain and Dewan Monir, have denied their involvement in illegal fishing activities. They claim their ghats were closed before the ban and attribute the uncontrolled situation to the administration's failure.

The Hizla Upazila Fisheries Department faces significant challenges, with a budget of only Tk 1.5 lakh allocated for enforcing the ban across a vast 69-kilometer Hilsa sanctuary. This limited funding makes it difficult to sustain operations for more than three to four days.
